title: Azure SQL Database Connectivity
description: Connect applications to Azure SQL Database using connection strings, firewall rules, and Azure networking options.

data.text: Connecting to Azure SQL Database requires two things: **network access** (firewall rules or VNet integration) and a valid **connection string**. Unlike on-premises SQL Server, Azure SQL lives behind a managed firewall, so you must explicitly allow the IP addresses or virtual networks that need access.

Azure SQL uses firewall rules at the server and database level. Server-level rules allow IP addresses to reach all databases on the server. Database-level rules are more granular. You can also enable 'Allow Azure services and resources to access this server' for services like Azure Functions or App Service.

data.title: Add a Server Firewall Rule with Azure CLI
data.content: Allow a specific IP address to connect to the logical server
data.code:
az sql server firewall-rule create \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --server sqlserver-demo \
  --name AllowMyIP \
  --start-ip-address 203.0.113.10 \
  --end-ip-address 203.0.113.10

data.text: For production, avoid public endpoints entirely. Use **private endpoints** so your Azure SQL Database is reachable only from your virtual network. This removes exposure to the internet and simplifies firewall management.

terms.definition: An IP-based access control rule at the server or database level that determines who can connect.
A private IP address inside your VNet that maps to Azure SQL, removing the need for public access.
A semicolon-delimited set of key-value pairs that tells a client how to reach and authenticate to a database.

data.title: Encrypt=True Is Required
data.text: Azure SQL requires TLS encryption. Always include Encrypt=True and TrustServerCertificate=False in production connection strings to prevent downgrade attacks.

data.title: Exercise: Connect Securely
data.description: Connect to Azure SQL from an application using both firewall and private endpoint methods.
steps: Create an Azure SQL single database.
Add a firewall rule for your development IP.
Connect with Azure Data Studio and run a simple query.
Create a private endpoint and update the firewall to block public access.
Connect again using the private endpoint and confirm connectivity.
data.expectedOutcome: Successful connections using both public firewall and private endpoint methods.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Firewall rules control which IPs can reach Azure SQL.
Connection strings include server name, database, credentials, and encryption settings.
Private endpoints remove public exposure and are recommended for production.
Always enforce TLS encryption in connection strings.
data.takeaway: Connectivity to Azure SQL requires careful planning of network access and secure connection strings.
